tool_input.command: grep -rniE "decision|decided|ADR|policy" --exclude-dir=.git --include=*.md --include=*.yml --include=*.yaml --include=*.txt . | head -30; ls -R .github | head -30; head -5 LICENSE; git log --all --oneline | head; git notes list 2>/dev/null | head

mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/license.md <<'EOF'
# Source license

The project's source is licensed under the MIT License, as recorded in the `LICENSE` file at the repository root (Copyright (c) 2014-present Manuel Martínez-Almeida), and the changelog records that the MIT license was added and applied to every source file.
EOF
cat docs/policies/license.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/license.md`. It says the source is licensed under the MIT License.

The repo has no dedicated decision records (no ADRs or policy docs). The statement rests on two things I found:
- **`LICENSE`:** the file at the repository root is the MIT License, Copyright (c) 2014-present Manuel Martínez-Almeida.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** two entries record that MIT was added and applied to every source file ("MIT license in every file" and "Add MIT license").

I treated those as the project's recorded decision. Nothing in the repo records an alternative or a change, so the file mentions none. If you keep decisions somewhere outside the repo, tell me and I'll check the file against them.
